attempts.summary: Configured node1 (Alpine 3.23, sudo 1.9.17p2) so every sudo command is recorded to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp, and no longer reaches the general system log. Previously sudo used its compiled-in default of logging via syslog's authpriv facility straight into /var/log/messages. Added /etc/sudoers.d/sudo-logging with `Defaults !syslog`, `Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"`, `Defaults log_year`, `Defaults log_host`, validated with visudo -c, and pre-created the log file (root:root, 600). Verified sudo commands now write entries like `Sep  4 23:08:02 2026 : root : HOST=node1 ; PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=...` to the dedicated file while /var/log/messages received no further sudo entries. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, issued a background `reboot` so the ack returned before disconnect, confirmed the node dropped and came back, proved boot_id changed (cbb5f7ee... -> 45013fd5..., uptime ~16s), and confirmed post-restart that the sudoers drop-in persisted, previously logged entries were retained, new sudo commands continued logging correctly to the dedicated file, and none leaked to /var/log/messages.
